name: Mosapramine
summary: An antipsychotic medicine used mainly in Japan for schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders. It blocks dopamine and serotonin, and at higher doses it can cause movement side effects.
description: Mosapramine is a second-generation (atypical) antipsychotic that blocks dopamine D2 and D3 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. It is mainly prescribed in Japan for schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders. It works much like other atypical antipsychotics but blocks dopamine fairly strongly, so at higher doses it can cause movement side effects such as stiffness, shaking or restlessness (extrapyramidal symptoms, EPS).

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Mosapramine is a second-generation (atypical) antipsychotic with antagonistic activity at dopamine D2, D3, and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. It is primarily prescribed in Japan for schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders. It has a pharmacological profile similar to other atypicals but retains relatively strong dopamine antagonism, which can lead to extrapyramidal symptoms (EPS) at higher doses.
